dedupe_keys.name: bins business intent and network slicing correlations

description: BINS publishes business-intent descriptions, annotations and correlations between user intents and network slices for intent-based network management. The research team supplies CSV files and a small web interface in the article-linked Figshare deposit. That populated deposit states CC0 1.0 and is free to access. Its GitHub README links a second, identically titled Figshare item containing only a short note, which instead states CC BY 4.0. The two records should not be treated as interchangeable downloads. The companion code describes BERT-based named-entity recognition for extracting network intents and parameters, with no software licence identified in the inspected repository. The data have no stated geographic coverage or operational time step, and acquisition dates are not specified in the own landing metadata. They can calibrate intent-recognition components in network-configuration and digital-twin studies related to platform-ns-3. A caveat is that labelled language-to-slice mappings are not measurements of network capacity or proof that a requested configuration is feasible.
